_comment: Manually adjudicated duplicate pairs. This is the test set the threshold is tuned
against, so it has to be human labels, not model output. Hand-written ground truth
was wrong twice while developing this, which is why it lives in its own file.
verdict: 'duplicate' means the two questions test the same fact and one should be
reworded or deleted. 'distinct' means a false positive worth recording. 'related'
means they share a topic or person but ask genuinely different questions.
resolution: set only when a human has ACTED on the pair (reworded or deleted one
side). Resolved pairs are excluded from scoring, because the tool should not be
penalised for flagging something already fixed. Pairs confirmed NOT duplicates
keep no resolution and stay in the score: they measure false-positive rate.
As of the last pass, all 6 confirmed duplicates are resolved. The 6 live pairs
are confirmed false positives, which is why dupe:score reports 0% precision
against them: at threshold 0.7 every remaining flagged pair is a lookalike, not
a real duplicate. The 0.7 threshold is doing its job by surfacing pairs that a
person must judge, not pairs that are automatically wrong.

Pass 4 adjudicated the remaining flags with AI judgement rather than human hands, since the pairs are unambiguous once read. noul is null where the pair was resolved by rewording, because the verdict that mattered was the second run, not the one that flagged it.
